explanation: The OK hand sign is understood in Singapore the same way as in most Western countries - meaning "okay" or "good" - without the offensive connotations it carries in places like Brazil or Turkey. It's used casually and isn't flagged as a taboo gesture in Singapore-specific etiquette guides.
local_tip: Feel free to use the OK sign casually; it's not considered rude or vulgar in Singapore the way it is in some other countries.

also_check.note: The OK sign is a vulgar insult, roughly equivalent to showing the middle finger.
The gesture can be read as a derogatory insult in some contexts.
